detail.longDescription: "In short, the race to RSI ends up being a race to eliminate the labs’ main avenue for capturing the value that they create — the fate of many past transformative technologies such as railroads, airlines, and fiber. The labs’ bet is that RSI produces a durable, decisive lead that escapes commoditization. My view is that there are two different improvement loops that have been conflated, and they will come apart. The efficiency improvement loop will accelerate, but a broader improvement loop that might lead to AGI or superintelligence will require ever-increasing amounts of compute, talent, data, and real-world feedback that can only come from gradual deployment, and the money to fund all this will have to come from massive revenue growth. And the irony is that the first improvement loop is undermining exactly that revenue growth. The premise in my chain of reasoning that I’m least confident in is #5 — that Jevons’ paradox will eventually stop being able to compensate for efficiency improvements. A few months ago I was much more of a believer in continued, nearly unbounded token volume growth, but the more I’ve thought about it the more skeptical I’ve become." https:// substack.com/@aisnakeoil/note/ c-376617176 # AI # BigTech # RSI # AGI # Automation # Productivity
